question: What does self-medication mean in everyday terms?

options.A: Participating in a clinical drug trial supervised by researchers
options.B: Using medicines to treat self-recognized symptoms without a prescription
options.C: Receiving intravenous medications exclusively inside a hospital ward
options.D: Taking drugs strictly prescribed and monitored by a licensed physician

explanation: Self-medication simply means buying or taking drugs on your own to treat symptoms without getting a doctor's go-ahead first. You've got this! [learn more](GNS215_U4_T1#GNS215_U4_T1_h1)

question: Why is it risky to reuse old prescription drugs for a new sickness?

options.A: The current symptoms may stem from a completely different underlying condition
options.B: Old pills lose their physical shape and become impossible to swallow safely
options.C: Pharmacy laws strictly forbid keeping unused tablets in a home cabinet
options.D: Expired medications always turn into toxic chemical substances immediately

explanation: Just because malaria felt a certain way last month doesn't mean today's fever is malaria! Treating a new problem with old medicine can delay finding the real issue. [learn more](GNS215_U4_T1#GNS215_U4_T1_h1)

question: What is one of the biggest reasons people resort to self-medication in Nigeria?

options.A: Strict regulations that completely ban open-market drug sellers
options.B: An abundance of free prescription drugs available in rural areas
options.C: Mandatory government laws requiring citizens to buy drugs alone
options.D: Long waiting times and high costs at formal healthcare facilities

explanation: Let's be real—long queues and costly hospital bills make many people run straight to the chemist or local vendor for quick relief instead. [learn more](GNS215_U4_T1#GNS215_U4_T1_h2)

question: How do open drug markets make self-medication so easy?

options.A: They provide easy, unrestricted access to potent drugs without a prescription
options.B: They operate under strict government supervision to prevent drug abuse
options.C: They offer free laboratory tests to help patients choose the right drug
options.D: They employ clinical pharmacologists who safely evaluate every customer

explanation: Open markets let anyone walk in with cash and walk out with strong, serious medications—no questions asked by a medical professional. [learn more](GNS215_U4_T1#GNS215_U4_T1_h2)

question: Why is it dangerous to swallow strong painkillers to hide tummy ache?

options.A: It causes immediate and permanent blindness in all affected adults
options.B: It permanently lowers a patient's normal body temperature
options.C: It can delay the diagnosis of a serious condition like appendicitis
options.D: It automatically cures any underlying infection within a few hours

explanation: Pain is your body's warning alarm! Masking it with painkillers might trick you into thinking you're fine while a serious emergency like appendicitis gets worse. [learn more](GNS215_U4_T1#GNS215_U4_T1_h3)

question: A patient turns yellowish and has severe upper belly pain after mixing local herbs with paracetamol for weeks. What likely happened?

options.A: Drug-induced liver injury from combined metabolic toxicity
options.B: A complete blockage of the urinary tract by solid crystals
options.C: Sudden infection caused by drinking too much cold water daily
options.D: A normal, expected side effect of taking harmless herbal teas

explanation: The liver has to process everything we swallow. Combining heavy doses of drugs and potent herbal mixes overworks the liver and can cause serious damage. [learn more](GNS215_U4_T1#GNS215_U4_T1_h3)

question: Why does stopping your antibiotics halfway through a course cause drug resistance?

options.A: It immediately destroys all friendly bacteria inside the stomach
options.B: It causes the remaining tablets in the pack to expire faster
options.C: It triggers an allergic reaction when the drug is taken again
options.D: It leaves the strongest microbes alive to mutate and multiply

explanation: When you stop early, you only kill the weak germs. The tough ones survive, get smarter, and multiply—meaning that drug won't work for you next time! [learn more](GNS215_U4_T1#GNS215_U4_T1_h4)

question: Why is taking leftover antibiotics a bad idea when you catch a common cold?

options.A: Colds require heavy surgical intervention instead of drug therapy
options.B: Cold viruses are already completely immune to all human medicines
options.C: Antibiotics change into sweet syrups when exposed to cold air
options.D: Colds are caused by viruses, whereas antibiotics only target bacteria

explanation: Remember: antibiotics fight bacteria, not viruses. Taking them for a viral cold does zero good and only helps build resistance. [learn more](GNS215_U4_T1#GNS215_U4_T1_h4)

question: What is the best way for a nurse to ask a patient about their use of herbs and over-the-counter drugs?

options.A: Use open, non-judgmental questions to encourage honest answers
options.B: Scold them severely for endangering their health without a doctor
options.C: Assume they only take orthodox drugs prescribed at the hospital
options.D: Ignore herbal remedies because they do not affect medical drugs

explanation: Patients will clam up if you judge them. Keeping your tone warm and open builds trust so they'll tell you everything they've been taking. [learn more](GNS215_U4_T1#GNS215_U4_T1_h5)

question: Why do nurses need to specifically ask patients about local herbal mixtures during an assessment?

options.A: Hospital policy forbids patients from drinking any local fluids
options.B: Herbal mixtures are always chemically identical to paracetamol
options.C: Doctors refuse to treat anyone who has ever used local roots
options.D: Patients often do not consider herbs to be real medications

explanation: Many folks see herbs as everyday food or natural supplements, so they won't think to mention them unless you ask directly! [learn more](GNS215_U4_T1#GNS215_U4_T1_h5)

question: How can a nurse check if a patient truly understands how to take their new medicine?

options.A: Handing them a dense medical textbook to read overnight in bed
options.B: Asking a family member to sign a legal compliance waiver
options.C: Assuming they understand if they nod silently during the talk
options.D: Asking the patient to repeat the instructions back in their own words

explanation: The 'teach-back' method is a nursing favorite! Having them explain it back in plain words guarantees they actually got the message. [learn more](GNS215_U4_T1#GNS215_U4_T1_h6)

question: Which of these is a dangerous medication habit that you should warn patients against?

options.A: Checking expiration dates on packaging before swallowing pills
options.B: Reporting any unusual itching or rashes to your healthcare provider
options.C: Sharing your leftover antibiotics with sick family members
options.D: Completing the entire dose prescribed by a qualified doctor

explanation: Never share your drugs! Dosage needs vary from person to person, and what cures your infection could harm someone else. [learn more](GNS215_U4_T1#GNS215_U4_T1_h6)

question: What is the main goal of community health outreaches regarding self-medication?

options.A: Encouraging citizens to treat complex infections at home alone
options.B: Closing down all local patent medicine stores in rural towns
options.C: Educating the public on the dangers of unsupervised drug use
options.D: Selling cheap pharmaceutical products directly from hospital vans

explanation: Outreaches are all about grassroots education—helping everyday people understand why popping random pills without guidance can hurt them. [learn more](GNS215_U4_T1#GNS215_U4_T1_h7)

question: How does teaching communities about health help cut down on self-medication?

options.A: It lowers the market prices of imported pharmaceutical tablets
options.B: It gives every citizen a license to prescribe drugs to their neighbors
options.C: It helps people recognize when symptoms require a professional medical evaluation
options.D: It eliminates the need for hospitals by teaching home surgical techniques

explanation: When people know better, they seek professional help early instead of guessing solutions at home with dangerous drugs. [learn more](GNS215_U4_T1#GNS215_U4_T1_h7)
